question: Can a subclass directly access a `private` member variable declared in its superclass by identifier name?

options.text: Yes, because inheritance operates by textually copying parent source lines into the child class.
No, private members cannot be accessed directly by name in subclasses.
No, because private variables are not allocated in subclass instances at all.
Yes, all private members of a parent class are directly accessible in child class bodies.

explanation: Private members of a superclass are not visible to subclasses. A subclass can only access private superclass fields indirectly via public or protected accessor methods.

question: Does an object instance of a subclass physically contain the memory for the superclass's `private` instance fields?

options.text: No, a subclass object omits private parent fields to occupy less memory than the superclass.
No, private fields are completely excluded from subclass instances because subclasses cannot access them.
Yes, a subclass object contains all superclass fields in heap memory, including private fields.
Yes, but only if the subclass re-declares them as public to enable textual code copying.

explanation: A subclass object allocates space for all instance fields of its entire superclass hierarchy on the heap, including private fields, even though the subclass cannot refer to them directly by name.

question: When designing an application, when should a class use inheritance (`is-a`) rather than composition (`has-a`)?

options.text: Whenever a class needs helper utility functions from an unrelated third-party class.
When the new class represents a genuine subtype that can substitute for the parent everywhere.
Whenever the subclass needs to be smaller in memory footprint than the existing parent.
Whenever private members of the parent need to be directly modified in the child body.

explanation: Inheritance models an is-a relationship where the subclass is a specialized kind of the superclass and satisfies the substitution principle. Composition is preferred for code reuse without subtyping.

question: How does Java implement inheritance when compiling a subclass extending a superclass?

options.text: By linking the child class to the parent class hierarchy in bytecode without duplicating parent code.
By stripping private parent variables so the subclass instance stays smaller in memory.
By textually copying the parent class bytecode methods directly into the child class file.
By converting all superclass private fields into public fields inside the child class.

explanation: Java establishes an inheritance relationship via metadata links (super_class reference in the class file); it does not copy the superclass methods or bytecode into the subclass.

Engine and Radio private fields cannot be merged into a single subclass instance.
'{' expected: Java does not support multiple class inheritance using multiple extends clauses.

FieldWorker cannot inherit from BaseWorker because inheritance copies constructors textually.

G (subclass constructor executes without calling parent constructors)
G B A (subclass constructors execute top-down after parent bytecode copying)
